title: Scheme charts underlying polarized etale effectivity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $D$ be a polarized descent datum [def-trf-polarized-scheme-etale-descent-datum] for a jointly surjective etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, schemes $f_i:X_i\to U_i$ and invertible modules $L_i$, with its given affine-local ampleness. The index set $I$ may lie in an independent universe. There exist a scheme $Y$, a map $g:Y\to S$, and isomorphisms $e_i:Y\times_SU_i\simeq X_i$ satisfying $f_i e_i=\operatorname{pr}_{U_i}$. Write $q_i=\operatorname{pr}_Y e_i^{-1}$. On $R_{ij}=X_i\times_{U_i}(U_i\times_SU_j)$ with projection $p_i$, one has $q_i p_i=q_j p_j\theta_{ij}$. This concludes only the underlying scheme and its prescribed scheme transitions: no global ordinary line module or comparison of line modules is asserted.

source.place: Spaces Tags 02WW and 02WV; Spaces Descent Tags 04W8 and 0D3C: construct the quotient space, descend the polarization, and apply relative ampleness to obtain only the underlying scheme with all original charts. Descent Tag 023Q recovers charts outside a chosen small subcover.

proof.text: Choose, for each point of S, a member of the covering and a point above it. This gives a subfamily indexed in the scheme universe, still covering S. Restrict theta, lambda, the diagonal identities and the test-scheme cocycles to it. Dependencies: [def-trf-polarized-scheme-etale-descent-datum].

proof.text: Form the coproduct of its X charts and overlaps. Apply SchemeDescentCocycle.etale_relation: an overlap with equal base coordinates factors through the diagonal by pullback uniqueness, and the supplied four-map cocycle gives its three-map cocycle by constructing the fourth map with the pullback lift. The quotient sheaf of this small etale relation is an algebraic space by AlgebraicSpace.etale_relation_quotient, with the prescribed kernel pair. Dependencies: [lem-trf-scheme-descent-cocycle-etale-relation], [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient], [def-trf-algebraic-space], [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

proof.text: Apply scheme_descent_quotient_chart_isomorphism to recover the subfamily charts. For an arbitrary original index, base change to that U_i. Its overlaps with the subfamily cover U_i, and theta identifies the local quotient charts with the base changes of X_i. The cocycle makes these identifications agree; representable sheaf gluing makes them a unique isomorphism. Thus all original indices are retained. Dependencies: [lem-trf-scheme-descent-quotient-chart-isomorphism], [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent].

proof.text: Descend lambda on the small atlas by exists_lineModule_of_etale_descent. The identity and cocycle are exactly the given ones after the canonical tensor comparisons. Its ordinary restriction on each chart is the given L_i. Dependencies: [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent].

proof.text: The given ampleness over inverse images of affine base opens verifies representable_and_ample_of_etale_cover. The identity scheme test represents the algebraic space by Y over S. Transport its chart identifications to obtain e. Their kernel-pair identification gives the displayed theta equation. This argument also covers empty S and empty covers: their quotient and Y are empty. Dependencies: [lem-trf-algebraic-space-ample-local].

theorem exists_polarizedSchemeCharts
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} {U : I → Scheme.{u}}
    {uMap : ∀ i, U i ⟶ S} {X : I → Scheme.{u}} {f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U i}
    {L : ∀ i, (X i).Modules} {hL : ∀ i, Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible (L i)}
    (D : PolarizedSchemeEtaleDescentDatum S I U uMap X f L hL)
    : ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ S) (e : ∀ i, pullback g (uMap i) ≅ X i),
      (∀ i, (e i).hom ≫ f i = pullback.snd g (uMap i)) ∧
        ∀ i j,
          polarizedOverlapX U uMap X f i j ≫ (e i).inv ≫ pullback.fst g (uMap i) =
            (D.theta i j).hom ≫ polarizedOverlapX U uMap X f j i ≫
              (e j).inv ≫ pullback.fst g (uMap j)
